q-111029.name: Question 1
q-111029.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14218586/assets/b8150a85386a2ebea9119820d25f227a6cb33aef8dd09b519feef4e8f70a4013.png)

The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following is the graph of $y=2f(x)?$

(*Note: Figures not drawn to scale*)
q-111029.worked_solution:
To graph the function $y=2f(x),$ we take the graph of $y=f(x)$ and stretch it by factor of $2$ parallel to the $y$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $y$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $2.$

The resulting graph is the solid blue curve shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14218586/assets/25441696cb23dc9d8b8a1cf2fee67d6606034dc73882daeabd256b1f11ba31ec.png)

q-111185.name: Question 6
q-111185.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(3,6)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=\frac{1}{3}f(x)?$
q-111185.worked_solution:
The function $y=\frac{1}{3}f(x)$ represents a compression of the function $y=f(x)$ by a factor of $3$ parallel to the $y$-axis. This has the effect of dividing the $y$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $3.$

Therefore, the point $(3,6)$ on $f(x)$ is mapped to the point $(3,\frac{6}{3})=(3,2),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y=\frac{1}{3}f(x).$

q-81962.name: Question 7
q-81962.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(3,-3)$ lies on the curve $y=3f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=f(x)?$
q-81962.worked_solution:
The function $y=3f(x)$ represents a stretch of the function $y=f(x)$ by a factor of $3$ parallel to the $y$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $y$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $3.$

The point $Q(3,q)$ on $f(x)$ is mapped to the point $P(3,-3)$ on $y=3f(x).$ Since we know that the $y$-coordinate of $P$ is $3$ times the $y$-coordinate of $Q,$ we can form the following equation:

$$
3q=-3
$$

Solving this equation, we get $q=-1.$ Therefore, the coordinates of $Q$ are $(3,-1).$

q-81962.html:
Question 7
?

The point P with coordinates (3,−3) lies on the curve y=3f(x). Which of the following points must lie on y=f(x)?

a
(3,−1)
b
(1,−1)
c
(9,−1)
d
(3,−9)
e
(1,−3)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The function y=3f(x) represents a stretch of the function y=f(x) by a factor of 3 parallel to the y-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the y-coordinates of all points on y=f(x) by 3.

The point Q(3,q) on f(x) is mapped to the point P(3,−3) on y=3f(x). Since we know that the y-coordinate of P is 3 times the y-coordinate of Q, we can form the following equation:

3q=−3

Solving this equation, we get q=−1. Therefore, the coordinates of Q are (3,−1).
